one_liner: Single-header AVX2, multithreaded FAST-9 corner detector matching Rosten's output; 5.1x faster than single-threaded OpenCV cv::FAST (2016).
what_it_does: Implements the FAST-9 (9 contiguous pixels on the 16-pixel circle) corner test of Rosten and Drummond, with optional 3x3 non-maximal suppression, on an 8-bit grayscale buffer with arbitrary stride. The API is one function template, KFAST<multithread, nonmax>(data, cols, rows, stride, std::vector<Keypoint>&, threshold), that fills a vector of {x, y, score} structs; it is not a cv::FeatureDetector, so OpenCV users convert to cv::KeyPoint themselves. On the repo's test image its keypoints match Rosten's fast9_detect_nonmax and cv::FAST position for position.
how_it_is_fast: Each AVX2 iteration tests 32 candidate pixels: saturating add and subtract of the threshold, an XOR with 0x80 so signed byte compares act as unsigned, and the classic four-point (circle points 1, 5, 9, 13) rejection test whose movemask lets the loop skip 32 or 16 pixels at once. Surviving lanes run a branch-free 24-step consecutive-run count over the circle plus 8 wrap-around points with byte max accumulators. Corner scores use 16-bit min/max over all 16 nine-pixel arcs and a PHMINPOSUW horizontal reduction; non-max suppression works on a rolling three-row score buffer. The multithreaded mode splits the image into row bands with overlapping halo rows, one std::async thread per hardware thread (capped at rows/16).
when_to_use: FAST-9 corner detection on 8-bit grayscale frames on x86-64 with AVX2, where you control the input allocation (ORB-style front ends, visual odometry, feature tracking).
Large images and spare cores: the default multithreaded mode is where the 5x figure comes from.
When output must be identical to Rosten's reference FAST-9 with non-maximal suppression; the driver checks equality against both Rosten's code and cv::FAST.
Projects that want FAST without linking OpenCV: KFAST.h has no dependencies beyond the C++ standard library and immintrin.h.
when_not_to_use: Input buffers you cannot pad: tail columns are read with full 32-byte loads, so the last rows read up to about 30 bytes past the end of the image (issue #3, Valgrind 'Invalid read of size 32'); the maintainer says this crashes if the over-read reaches unmapped memory and recommends over-allocating by at least 32 bytes. Master is unfixed.
Non-AVX2 targets (ARM/NEON, older x86): there is no fallback, whereas current OpenCV cv::FAST has universal-intrinsic SIMD and a runtime-dispatched AVX2 path and runs everywhere.

Small images, per-frame latency budgets or already-threaded pipelines: multithreaded mode launches fresh std::async threads on every call; use the single-threaded template there, for which no measurement is published.
Other FAST variants (FAST-10, 11 or 12, which the bundled Rosten folder does provide) or ROI masks: only the 9-of-16 test is implemented.
Anything needing maintenance: last code change January 2019, and PR #4 (memcpy tail that removes the over-read) has been open since July 2019.

integration.dependencies: none for KFAST.h; the test driver main.cpp needs OpenCV (core, features2d, highgui, imgcodecs) and pthreads, and uses legacy OpenCV C-API constants (CV_LOAD_IMAGE_GRAYSCALE, CV_WINDOW_NORMAL)
integration.min_toolchain: C++11 per README (Makefile builds with g++ -std=gnu++17 -march=native); MSVC also stated as supported; GCC/Clang need -mavx2 plus BMI1 (_tzcnt_u32, _blsr_u32); KFAST.h calls memset without including <cstring>
integration.platforms: x86-64 with AVX2 and BMI1; Linux (g++) and Windows (MSVC) per README; no runtime dispatch or scalar fallback
integration.thread_safety: not documented; by inspection there is no global state, each call allocates its own scratch buffer with _mm_malloc and writes only the caller's vector, so concurrent calls on different outputs are safe
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same keypoints as cv::FAST(img, kps, thresh, true) with the 9/16 pattern and as Rosten's fast9_detect_nonmax, but a different signature and Keypoint struct, and the input buffer must be padded by 32 bytes

gotchas: Out-of-bounds read: for most image widths the last processCols call on the last processed row loads 32 bytes from the bottom image row starting a few columns before its end; results are masked so output is unaffected, but ASan/Valgrind flag it and an image ending at a page boundary can segfault (issue #3, closed in April 2019 with the advice to over-allocate, no code change).

The headline is multi-threaded against single-threaded: main.cpp defaults to KFAST_multithread = true while cv::FAST and Rosten's code run on one thread. The README's single-threaded '60%' and main.cpp's '40-60% over the reference implementation' have no published run; 'reference' cannot mean Rosten's code, because in the same screenshot OpenCV is already 4.2x faster than Rosten (derived from page data). A KFAST.h comment ('2000 -> 2600 microseconds without forced inlining') hints at about 2 ms per call on the test image, roughly 1.6x faster than OpenCV's 3.3 ms (derived), but it does not say which threading mode.

The only first-party numbers (results.jpg) were captured on 2016-09-12, before the October 2016 'horizontal AVX shuffle' performance commit and the January 2019 PR #2 fix, against an OpenCV build of unknown version; OpenCV's cv::FAST has since gained a runtime-dispatched AVX2 path (fast.avx2.cpp, split out of fast.cpp in October 2017), so the gap to a current OpenCV is unmeasured.

Before PR #2 (January 2019) the tail mask could evaluate 1 << 32 (undefined behaviour), which the maintainer said misses corners in the last 32 columns for affected widths; in current master the shift amount is at most 31 for any width of 6 columns or more, and narrower images give a negative shift (also undefined).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: No other FAST detector is catalogued; the listed siblings (bilinear_filter_simd, SIMD_TriangleAABB, the author's Leftpack and FastArrayOps) are unrelated SIMD kernels. Against the real incumbent, cv::FAST, pick KFAST only when you have AVX2, can pad input buffers, and want multithreaded FAST without OpenCV.
verified_claims_summary: The only first-party run (results.jpg, a 2016 console screenshot of main.cpp; one test image, threshold 50, non-max on, mean of 1000 calls after 150 warm-ups) shows multi-threaded KFAST at 646.711 us per call against single-threaded cv::FAST at 3299.35 us (5.1x) and Rosten's scalar fast9_detect_nonmax at 13750.4 us (21.3x), all 8361 keypoints identical; CPU, compiler and OpenCV version are not stated. A third-party run on an unspecified Mac, posted in the PR #4 thread in July 2019 with that PR's branch, gave 717.865 us against 2918.54 us (4.07x) and 13099.9 us (18.25x).
status_note: Abandoned since January 2019 (the 2021 commit only adds the MIT LICENSE; the bundled Rosten folder is BSD-3-Clause; PR #4 unmerged), but a single MIT header that is easy to vendor if you pad input buffers by 32 bytes or apply PR #4's memcpy tail; evidence stays first-party and mixes thread counts.
